The Authentic Name

Scholarly reference for Yām

Scholarly Transliteration

Yām

The original script for this canaanite name has not yet been added to PUNYCODEX. The form shown is a scholarly transliteration.

ASCII Constraint

YAM

Stripped of its identity, the name was reduced to plain Latin letters. The original orthography — stress, length, breathing — was erased by systems that only understand A-Z.

Unicode Restoration

Yām

The Unicode restoration recovers what ASCII destroyed. This is philological accuracy — not decoration. The domain encodes to Punycode, but the browser displays the truth.

Valid Scholarly Variations
Yammu

Each variant is an attested scholarly orthography. No domain is claimed here; these are documented Unicode forms for scholarly reference.

Name Senses
Primary sense The Ugaritic sea god, opponent of Baal in the Baal Cycle.
Mythological Represents the chaotic, untamable primordial waters surrounding the ordered world.

The name carries more than one valid sense. The primary sense is the figure or role; the etymology is the older linguistic root.

Punycode Encoding
yām.com → xn--ym-dla.com

The non-ASCII characters in Yām are encoded while the ASCII remains visible. To the DNS, it is Punycode. To humanity, it is Yām. PUNYCODEX does not claim this domain is available; always verify status with a registrar.

02

Etymology

The deep ancestry of Yām

proto-semitic *yamm- "sea, ocean"

From Proto-Semitic *yamm- "sea"; cognate with Hebrew yām יָם. In Ugaritic myth Yām is a chaotic sea deity defeated by Baal.

hebrew yām cognate Sea in Biblical Hebrew arabic yamm cognate Sea in Arabic
attested

Tier Classification

Why Yām is classified as Tier-2 Macron-Preserving

The Canaanite original Yām contains only length (macron vowel). This makes it a single-tier Tier-2 name. The Unicode restoration preserves what can be preserved — honoring the single feature that distinguishes it from plain ASCII.
